- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 2–3 periods.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast if sentiment remains flat or slightly bullish.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) and price is near 30-day low, model often misses support; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to avoid false bottom.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–2% for next 2–3 periods to avoid overbought trap.
